key: A lost update is two people writing
name: ch07_cashbox_register_line_vs_page_rule
alt: Two cashiers overwrite the same register line on the left; on the right two cashiers write on different lines and together drain the cash box below the minimum.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves set at the back counter of a busy Indian cloth shop with a big open cash register book on a wooden counter and a steel cash box beside it. LEFT panel: two cashiers, a young man in a striped shirt and an older woman in a green sari, both lean over the register and write on the very same line at the same moment, their two pens touching and their numbers scribbled over each other into an ink smudge; a small red cross sits beside the smudged line to show one entry is lost. RIGHT panel: the same two cashiers each first read the whole page, shown by two dotted gaze lines sweeping across it, and each writes a withdrawal on a different line, one near the top and one near the bottom, both looking satisfied. Below the book, the steel cash box is open and nearly empty, holding only a couple of notes, and a small sign taped to the box shows a minimum line with a red exclamation badge because the two withdrawals together pushed it under the limit. Two thin arrows from the two separate lines meet at the cash box. Warm tube-light glow, rolls of cloth on shelves behind, calm faces that have not noticed the problem. Labels: "LOST UPDATE" at the top of the left panel, "WRITE SKEW" at the top of the right panel, and "RULE BROKEN" beside the near-empty cash box.

name: ch07_invigilator_magnifier_vs_seatmap
alt: One invigilator slowly compares two answer sheets line by line with a magnifying glass, while another quickly cancels papers just because the students sat side by side.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves inside the same school exam hall after the exam, with wooden desks, a ceiling fan and a blackboard. LEFT panel: an invigilator in a cotton sari with spectacles on a chain sits at a table, holding a large magnifying glass over two answer sheets laid side by side; thin dotted lines link matching lines on the two sheets, one by one. A tall stack of unchecked papers rises beside her and a wall clock above shows the hands having moved a long way, with a small hourglass by her elbow; she looks careful and tired, and only one pair of sheets gets a red stamp. RIGHT panel: a second invigilator, a brisk man in a half-sleeve shirt, stands in front of a simple seating chart on an easel, a grid of desks where pairs of neighbouring seats are circled. He stamps CANCEL on papers quickly; the pile is done, but one cancelled student, a girl with plaits holding her sheet, looks upset with a small question-mark badge, because she sat next to someone but did not copy. A small stopwatch near him shows a short time. Bright morning daylight, fair and slightly comic mood. Labels: "FINE-GRAINED" at the top of the left panel, "COARSE" at the top of the right panel, and "SLOW" under the left invigilator's tall stack.

key: Many clerks book seats on the same train
name: ch07_train_chart_clerks_take_turns
alt: Several railway clerks crowd one big reservation chart and scribble over each other, while on the right they book one at a time in a neat queue.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in an Indian railway reservation office with a big printed train chart pinned to a board, rows of berth boxes for coaches S1 and S2. LEFT panel: three clerks in white shirts crowd the chart at once, each reaching in with a pen. Two of them write on the same berth box and their writing overlaps into a scribble; another box shows a booking being rubbed out by its own clerk while a passenger looking at it points in confusion. Above the chart, two small inset bubbles show the most visual troubles: one bubble with a tally reading "10" and two arrows both turning it into "9", and one bubble with berth "23" marked free and then suddenly filled by a new booking with a red exclamation badge. The clerks look busy and do not see each other's pens. RIGHT panel: the same three clerks stand in a short orderly queue holding token numbers 1, 2 and 3; only the first clerk writes on the chart, the others wait calmly, and every box on the chart is clean with green ticks. Warm tube-light, ceiling fan, a train timetable on the wall. Labels: "ANOMALIES" at the top of the left panel, "SERIALIZABLE" at the top of the right panel, and "TAKE TURNS" under the queue.
